subject: FlowWorks
advisory: Full-list speed with FlowWorks loaded stays near the other mods' cost (the 346 to ~120 TPS drop is the floor's tick_cost line, measured on the walk)

leaves.oracle_proposed: blind reader on captures orders the four depths and names them dug ground; a job timer reads the dig in game hours
leaves.tier_reason: an on-screen look and a live state change: needs a running map, which a dev quicktest colony gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player, at play zoom in daylight, sees a dug canal as a channel cut into the ground, dry or filled, at every depth D1-D4 and in each of the four directions; the depths read apart by their wall faces, and a colonist takes hours, not seconds, to dig one. It must not read as a path, a floor or a built wall.
leaves.scenario: Designate a 1x8 canal and a ladder of pads at D1, D2, D3, D4 on sand and on soil; a colonist digs one cell; capture each pad dry and filled with water at play zoom, N/E/S/W runs.
false_pass: the depths are the same texture with a number in the inspect pane
the dig finishes in one tick
leaves.red: every depth draws the same flat tile, so a D1 ditch and a D4 pit look alike

leaves.oracle_proposed: per-cell fill read each 250 ticks: the front advances monotonically and tar's front is behind water's at every read; captures show it
leaves.tier_reason: an on-screen look and a live state change: needs a running map, which a dev quicktest colony gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player opening a canal onto a source watches the liquid front move cell by cell along the channel and stop at its end, never spilling onto the banks; a tar front visibly lags a water front opened at the same moment.
leaves.scenario: Two parallel 1x12 D2 canals, one cut into a water body and one into a tar body, opened on the same tick; capture every 250 ticks until both stand full.
false_pass: the whole canal fills on one tick
tar and water arrive together
leaves.red: the canal fills all at once, or the liquid also covers the bank cells

leaves.oracle_proposed: blind reader sorts fill tiers and names liquids from captures; state read matches each capture

leaves.experience: The player at play zoom tells how full a canal is (dry, very shallow, half, full) and with what liquid (water, tar, chemfuel, slime), and that it is the same liquid as the body it came from; half a metre of water reads as silty shallows, not clear deep water.
leaves.scenario: Five parallel D5 runs filled to F0..F4, and four runs of different liquids at the same fill, beside their source bodies.
false_pass: only the inspect pane says the fill
every liquid draws as water
leaves.red: a half-full and a full canal draw identically, or tar draws as water

leaves.oracle_proposed: bridge read of all cells' surface level: max minus min at most one step; capture shows no seam

leaves.experience: The tester reading every cell of a still connected body (canal, pit and pond joined) sees one surface level, within one decilitre-step, after it settles; the player sees no stepped water in it.
leaves.scenario: Dig a canal joining a pond to a D4 pit across uneven ground; let it settle 2 game hours; read every cell's level.
false_pass: levels equal because every cell was set by hand
level equal only in the cells the probe reads
leaves.red: the far end of the canal stands lower than the pond forever

leaves.oracle_proposed: body report volume and drawn shoreline cell count before/after; Endless readout on the edge lake; captures

leaves.scenario: A 200-square dug pond feeds a 60-cell moat; capture before, after the fill, after a further draw by a Sink tap to empty, then each day of rain for 5 days; a second moat fed from an edge-touching lake.
false_pass: the pond's number drops but its drawn shore never moves
refill is instant
leaves.red: the pond stays full however much the moat takes

leaves.oracle_proposed: blind reader on captures: hose vs cord, plump vs flat, four styles apart; flow state read matches

leaves.oracle_proposed: per step: swim state and rest drop, moat litres fall to the drain, raiders' paths out refused, prisoner status after capture, chemfuel litres leave the tank into the moat, fire on moat cells; capture sequence for him
leaves.tier_reason: a raid with pathing, swimming and capture runs only in a played map; the minimal list plus FlowWorks isolates it
leaves.experience: The player defending a fortress watches the whole moat sequence at play zoom: raiders swim a deep water moat under a raised drawbridge and tire; the sluice opens and the moat drains fast; the raiders are held in the pit, cannot climb out, and are taken as prisoners from the rim; then chemfuel is pumped in from above and lit, and the moat burns. It must not read as raiders walking across, a moat that empties by magic, or fire that is not the liquid.
leaves.scenario: The flagship map: fortress, one deep D4 water moat fed from a pond, a raised drawbridge, a sluice to a drain pit, a chemfuel tank and pump at the rim; a raid of 6 arrives; the player opens the sluice, captures two, pumps chemfuel and tosses a flame.
